questions.text: Which device primarily forwards packets between networks?
questions.explanation: A router connects and forwards traffic between different networks.

questions.text: What is the main job of an Ethernet switch?
options: Connect wired devices within a LAN
questions.explanation: A switch interconnects wired devices on a local network.

questions.text: Which medium usually provides a wired LAN connection?
questions.explanation: Ethernet cabling is a common wired LAN connection method.

questions.text: Why might a classroom use a switch as well as a router?
options: Both devices do exactly the same job in every case
A router can never connect to a switch
The switch connects local wired devices; the router connects networks
questions.explanation: Switches serve local wired connectivity; routers provide network-to-network forwarding.

questions.text: Why can Wi-Fi become unreliable through several thick walls?
options: Wireless signals can weaken and encounter interference
The router loses its IP permanently
questions.explanation: Distance and barriers can reduce wireless signal quality.

questions.text: How can one home gateway serve as a router, switch, and access point?
options: Every home contains three hidden computers
It can combine several networking functions in one device
questions.explanation: Consumer gateways frequently integrate several networking functions.

questions.text: A desktop has an Ethernet port and sits beside a switch. Which connection is sensible?
options: HDMI cable to the internet provider
Ethernet cable from desktop to switch
questions.explanation: An Ethernet cable carries wired network traffic.

questions.text: A phone needs wireless access to a school LAN. Which component provides the wireless entry point?
questions.explanation: An access point lets wireless devices join the LAN.

questions.text: A house loses power to its Wi-Fi router. What is the first sensible action?
options: Check that the router has power and restart only when appropriate
questions.explanation: Start by verifying the affected equipment is powered and functioning.

questions.text: Wired computers work, but tablets cannot join Wi-Fi. Where should you investigate first?
options: Every Ethernet cable must be broken
Wireless access point or Wi-Fi settings
questions.explanation: A wireless-specific fault is more likely when wired access still works.

questions.text: An Ethernet PC shows no link light while nearby PCs work. What is the best initial check?
options: Assume the entire internet is offline
Check that its cable is firmly connected and try a known-good port or cable
questions.explanation: A single failed wired link suggests checking its local cable or port.

questions.text: A team needs reliable connectivity for fixed desktop PCs and mobility for tablets. What is the best design?
options: Wi-Fi only for every device without exception
No router and no access point
Ethernet for desktops and Wi-Fi for tablets on the same LAN
questions.explanation: A combined wired and wireless LAN matches the different device needs.
